messages:
alim_sales: Heads-up: LumaTech POC blocked. Their console shows inconsistent trace linking and around 25% of Splunk export rows are missing trace_id. They also hit repeated 429s during a scripted bulk demo. Can we swarm for a quick fix? :rotating_light:

oscar_se: on it. Can you paste one redacted request + forwarder log from their ticket? Even a single sample helps determine if the trace header reaches our gateway.

alim_sales: pasted from their ticket (redacted):
```
POST /v1/chat 200
Headers: { Authorization: Bearer REDACTED, X-Trace-Id: c0ffee42, traceparent: 00-c0ffee42000000000000000000000001-01 }
Client log:
[2026-03-20T22:41:03Z] WARN status=429 reason=rate_limit id=req-LT-01 trace=c0ffee42
[2026-03-20T22:41:04Z] INFO forwarder.hec send status=accepted trace=
```

oscar_se: pattern suggests header present when request hit us but the forwarded HEC event sometimes lacks trace. Two common causes: (1) exporter didn't inject `metadata.trace_id` into batched export events, or (2) their forwarder/sampler strips headers under load.

mira_sre: I can run quick checks: scan exporter logs for missing metadata.trace_id for org=lumatech, inspect Splunk HEC connector sampling rules, and temporarily raise the POC token qps to reduce 429s during the demo. Need short approval to bump.

alim_sales: I can approve a 20-minute bump for the demo. They're live in 30 minutes.

mira_sre: ok I raised token qps to 6rps for org=lumatech for 20m and turned on verbose export logging.

deploy-bot: runtime change scheduled: poc-qps-bump -> org-lumatech (owner: mira_sre). Canary: 3% traffic.

deploy-bot: canary OK. change rolled to 100% for org-lumatech.

oscar_se: small mitigation I can deploy: exporter will now canonicalize trace id in every exported event by checking in order: event.metadata.trace_id || X-Trace-Id || traceparent (extract trace id). If found, exporter sets `metadata.trace_id` and `exporter.trace_source=<header|traceparent|metadata>`. Deploying a canary now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: exporter-canonicalize-trace v0.1.0 -> p-prod-canary (owner: oscar_se)

deploy-bot: canary health: 9/9 checks passed, 2% traffic routed.

oscar_se: canary verified: exported events now include metadata.trace_id=c0ffee42 and exporter.trace_source=header for those requests; Splunk HEC shows matching ids. Missing-trace rows dropped from ~24% -> ~2% on canary subset.

alim_sales: great. What should I send to the customer immediately?

mira_sre: short runbook to share with LumaTech ops:
1) Ensure any intermediate forwarder preserves the incoming trace header (`X-Trace-Id` or `traceparent`) or writes the trace id into event metadata as `metadata.trace_id`.
2) When configuring a Splunk HEC drain, set `map_trace_id=metadata.trace_id` so exported rows include the trace id column. Example curl to create drain:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/drains \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <org-token>" \
  -d '{"type":"splunk_hec","url":"https://splunk.lumatech:8088/services/collector","token":"HEC_TOKEN","map_trace_id":"metadata.trace_id"}'
```
3) For short demos, request `trace_sampling: full` or a temporary `token_qps` bump to avoid 429s. Note `trace_sampling: full` increases exported volume.

david_security: security note: confirm Splunk HEC endpoint uses TLS and that the HEC token is scoped to ingest-only. Also record customer approval for the 20-minute qps bump in the security approvals log. I'll attach to the POC security questionnaire.

alim_sales: LumaTech confirmed TLS + ingest-only HEC token and approved the 20m bump. I'll schedule a quick 15-min ops pairing to walk through header passthrough and the HEC config. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
